title: An AI Marking Case Study: From Four Hours to Twenty Minutes
author: Daisy Christodoulou
summary: Daisy Christodoulou describes a case study from King Edward VI School, Stratford-upon-Avon, in which English teacher Amaryllis Barton used No More Marking's Comparative Judgement platform—enhanced with AI—to assess 26 Year 9 students' non-fiction writing in under 20 minutes. Traditional marking of equivalent quality would have taken four or more hours. Amaryllis performed 26 paired judgements herself (viewing each script twice) while AI handled the remaining 90% of comparisons, producing a judging reliability of 0.88. The AI automatically generated personalized feedback for each student, while Amaryllis added her own audio comments via a microphone tool that transcribes and polishes speech into student-friendly language. This hybrid model maintains meaningful human engagement with student writing—every script is seen at least twice by the teacher—while dramatically reducing workload. Christodoulou argues this addresses the central concern about AI assessment: that it might cause teachers to disengage from student work, which could undermine student motivation. A key innovation is that individual teachers can now run their own single-class assessments with nationally calibrated data, without requiring hundreds of participating schools.
points: * The platform uses Comparative Judgement—teachers make paired 'which is better?' decisions rather than applying rubrics—allowing rank-ordered assessment that is both more reliable and less cognitively burdensome than traditional marking. * AI handled 90% of the paired judgements, with the human teacher completing 10%; the design ensures every student script is seen twice by a human, doubling the teacher engagement of traditional rubric-marking. * Audio feedback (teacher speaks observations aloud; AI transcribes and polishes) delivers personalized human feedback at far greater speed than typing, making detailed responses feasible within tight time constraints. * The hybrid system achieved a judging reliability of 0.88 out of 1.0, with 62% human-AI agreement—acceptable given the class's narrow ability range and validated by the teacher's review of disagreements. * Adding AI to the platform removes the need for hundreds of schools to participate in national assessments, making individually calibrated writing assessment accessible to a single teacher with one class.
quotes: Adding in the AI makes it possible for just one teacher to complete all the required human judging.

People quite rightly worry that AI assessment means teachers stop engaging with student writing, and that this could have a knock-on effect on student engagement. Why bother working hard on a piece of writing when your teachers can't be bothered to read it? But in the system we have designed, every script is seen twice by a human, which is double what happens with traditional non-AI rubric based assessment.
While judging, teachers can click a microphone button and speak their feedback. The AI transcribes what they say, polishes it and turns it into a written comment in student friendly language.

That is incredibly rapid. I used to be a secondary English teacher, and using traditional marking, I would estimate that it would take me at least four hours, maybe more, to produce this level of quality personalised feedback and reliable scores.
The audio feedback is not AI feedback, it is human feedback and it shows the student that the teacher has read their work. But because speaking is much faster than typing, it is much more efficient.
